findings.message: scan.rs abandons Rust's Result/`?` idiom wholesale: all 8 candidate-gather helpers (gather_hnsw_candidates l.272, scan_ivf_structured l.487, scan_ivf_aq l.603, scan_ivf_aq_split l.714, scan_ivf_aq_split_v7 l.847, scan_ivf_aq_split_sq8 l.1026, scan_ivf_aq_split_rabitq l.1133, gather_symqg_candidates l.334) return a plain `-> Vec<(i64, f64)>` instead of `-> Result<Vec<(i64, f64)>, String>`, so `?` cannot propagate and every fallible sub-call is a hand-written `match { Ok(v) => v, Err(e) => pg_sys::error!(...) }` — C-style check-and-bail, not idiomatic Rust (The Rust Book ch.9 'Recoverable Errors with Result' — the `?` operator exists precisely to remove this boilerplate). The crate's OWN convention is the opposite: columnar_agg.rs:939 and columnar.rs:1524 use an inner `(|| -> Result<T,String> { ... })()` closure with `?` throughout and exactly ONE `Err(e) => pg_sys::error!` boundary at the `#[pg_guard]` extern-"C-unwind" edge. scan.rs is the crate outlier. This is idiomaticity-adjacent to the `code` pillar finding at src/am/scan.rs:289 (source_tool 'claude:code', message opens 'untyped pg_sys::error! for user-input query-dimension mismatch') but is NOT a duplicate: that finding is about the error TYPE (XX000 vs typed 22023 err_input) at 3 user-input sites; this finding is about the control-flow idiom (Result/`?` discarded across all 8 gather helpers, forcing the repeated match blocks).
findings.remediation: Change the 8 gather helpers to `-> Result<Vec<(i64, f64)>, String>` and replace each `match r { Ok(v)=>v, Err(e)=>pg_sys::error!(...) }` with `r?` (map inner String errors as needed); keep exactly ONE `match gather(...) { Ok(v)=>v, Err(e)=>pg_sys::error!("...: {e}") }` at the `amrescan`/`amgettuple` #[pg_guard] boundary — the pattern columnar_agg.rs:939 already uses.

findings.evidence: `grep -n 'if page::ivf_is_v' src/am/scan.rs` returns exactly 5 branches (l497 v7, l501 v4, l505 v5, l509 v6, l513 v8) inside scan_ivf_structured (l487-517). Each new IVF format required adding: (a) a branch here, (b) a scan_ivf_aq_split_* fn (`grep -n '^unsafe fn scan_ivf_aq' src/am/scan.rs` = 5 defs: l603/714/847/1026/1133), (c) a page-side ivf_is_vN + read_ivf_aq_meta_split_* + writer, (d) an or_else arm in page::ivf_list_count. `grep -c ah_score_block src/am/scan.rs` = 5 (the Stage-1 AH-prune loop is repeated near-verbatim across the split variants; only Stage-2 rerank differs). This is the OCP 'type-tag ladder edited on every new case' signal with demonstrated churn — NOT speculative (>=2 real variants). Counterweight (KISS): an explicit central dispatch on a persisted format tag is a defensible, discoverable design; a trait/registry could over-abstract on-disk formats whose Stage-2 genuinely differs. Hence MEDIUM/internal, not a boundary-seam HIGH. Distinct from the maintainability pillar's `dry_duplicated_version_probe` (which flags the ivf_is_v* probe bodies); this flags the DISPATCH being open-for-modification.
findings.message: OCP (Open/Closed, Meyer 1988 / Martin ASD:PPP ch.11): the IVF on-disk format dispatch in scan_ivf_structured is a hardcoded if-ladder over version tags (ivf_is_v4/v5/v6/v7/v8) that MUST be edited for every new persisted format, alongside a parallel version-tagged scan_ivf_aq_split_* function. The dispatch site is not closed for modification: v3..v8 is six historical edits of the same switch.
findings.remediation: Introduce a closed extension point for IVF formats, e.g. resolve the persisted version once and dispatch through one `IvfScanFormat` trait (meta-read + Stage-2 rerank) with a shared Stage-1 AH-prune skeleton, so a new format adds an impl instead of editing the scan_ivf_structured ladder + duplicating the prune loop.

findings.remediation: After the count check in from_bytes add `if neighbors.iter().flatten().flatten().any(|&nb| nb >= n) { return Err("theodb hnsw: neighbor references an out-of-bounds vector".into()); }` (mirroring ann/ivf.rs:416).

findings.evidence: from_bytes l66-91 only checks `if b.len() != adj_end` (l74) then reads `adj` (u32 node ids) and `offsets` (u64) verbatim with NO bound check. expand l115-118 indexes `self.offsets[node]`/`[node+1]` then `for &nbr in &self.adj[a0..a1]` and re-enters the frontier (l123) / `is(&visited, ni)` (l120) with the unvalidated nbr; expand_multi l181-183 and ppr l245-247 have the same unvalidated `self.adj[a0..a1]` + `seen[ni]`. A non-monotonic offset (a0>a1 or a1>adj.len()) or a nbr>=nnodes -> OOB slice/index panic across the C boundary. The persisted CSR lives in the ordinary catalog TABLE theodb.graph_csr (l29-37) — a wider tamper/corruption surface than an index page (a role with UPDATE on it, or on-disk corruption, supplies the bytes). from_bytes is a live production path (load_cached_csr:406 on every cold graph_expand/graph_ppr). Sibling ann/ivf.rs:416 performs the analogous adjacency validation; graph.rs omits it. Also l71-73 `noff*8`/`total_adj*4` can overflow usize for a corrupt huge nnodes.
findings.message: PRINCIPLE (validate untrusted input at the deserialization boundary): Csr::from_bytes validates only the total blob length, not that `adj` node ids are < nnodes nor that `offsets` are monotonic and bounded — a crafted/corrupt theodb.graph_csr bytea then drives out-of-bounds indexing in expand/expand_multi/ppr. Tainted flow: theodb.graph_csr.csr bytea -> load_cached_csr -> Csr::from_bytes -> self.offsets[node]/self.adj[a0..a1]/seen[ni].
findings.remediation: In Csr::from_bytes verify offsets are non-decreasing with offsets[nnodes]==total_adj and every `adj` entry < nnodes (typed Err otherwise), using checked_mul for the noff*8 / total_adj*4 size arithmetic — before returning Ok(Csr{...}).

findings.evidence: l264-266 `Spi::get_one_with_args::<String>("SELECT format('SELECT (%I)::bigint AS s, (%I)::bigint AS d FROM %s WHERE %I IS NOT NULL AND %I IS NOT NULL', $1,$2,$3,$1,$2)", &[src_col.into(), dst_col.into(), edge_rel.into()])`: the columns ($1=src_col, $2=dst_col) use `%I` (quoted) but the relation ($3=edge_rel) uses `%s` (raw substitution), then l276 `client.select(&scan_sql, None, &[])` executes it. edge_rel is a caller-supplied `text` arg (public wrapper theodb.graph_build(edge_rel text,...) l561); the `::regclass::oid` cast only runs later at persist (l349), AFTER the vulnerable scan. The l262 comment falsely claims 'Injection-safe: identifiers quoted via Postgres format('%I')'. Mitigations: the graph_* functions are REVOKE'd from PUBLIC (l543,l575-584) and run with invoker rights (not SECURITY DEFINER), so this is not privilege escalation — but a granted second-order caller passing untrusted text as edge_rel executes attacker SQL with the caller's role.
findings.message: PRINCIPLE (OWASP A03 Injection / parameterize-or-quote every identifier): build_csr interpolates the untrusted `edge_rel` text argument with `%s` (RAW, unquoted) instead of `%I`/regclass into the scan query and runs it via client.select BEFORE any regclass validation. Tainted flow: theodb.graph_build(edge_rel text) request arg -> build_csr -> client.select(&scan_sql).
findings.remediation: Feed the relation through regclass so PG renders a safely-quoted reference: pass `($3)::regclass` into format's `%s` (e.g. `SELECT format('... FROM %s ...', $1,$2,($3)::regclass,$1,$2)`), OR validate `edge_rel::regclass` before build_csr runs the scan.

findings.evidence: build_csr allocates dense arrays keyed by the max node id: `let nn = nnodes as usize;` with `nnodes = (maxn+1)` (l302) then `let mut deg = vec![0u64; nn + 1];` (l306), `let mut offsets = vec![0u64; nn + 1];` (l311) and `let mut adj = vec![0u32; acc as usize];` (l319). Node ids come from arbitrary user bigint columns, so a legal graph with few edges but a max id near u32::MAX allocates ~34 GB (the code's own test comment at l1112-1120 documents this OOM); the u32 guard (l291) only bounds it AT u32::MAX, not below it.
findings.message: Scalability/Data Partitioning — missing_required: CSR memory is O(max_node_id), not O(nodes+edges); a sparse-but-high-id graph OOMs the backend
findings.remediation: Remap arbitrary node ids to a dense 0..nnodes ordinal space via a HashMap during build (store the id<->ordinal map alongside the CSR), so offsets/adj scale with the DISTINCT node count, not the max id.

findings.evidence: graph_refold does `Spi::get_two_with_args::<String,String>(...).ok();` (l.361-365) then `match cols { Some((Some(s),Some(d))) => ..., _ => crate::pg::err_input("theodb.graph_refold: no persisted CSR for this edge relation (run graph_build first)") }` (l.366-371). `.ok()` collapses `Err(spi::Error)` into `None`, so a real SPI failure is reported to the user as 'run graph_build first' — a wrong remediation for an unrelated failure.
findings.message: SPI Result discarded via .ok() masks a real execution error as 'no CSR'. Unbreakable Rule 8 / error-handling.md §5: a Result carrying a real error must not be dropped and re-mapped to a generic/misleading message; distinguish 'no rows' (Ok(None)) from an execution error (Err) and fail clear. The same masking pattern recurs at l.383 (load_cached_csr -> err_unsupported 'no persisted CSR') and l.396/400 (-> 'persisted CSR row vanished mid-query').
findings.remediation: Match the Result explicitly: on Err(e) propagate the real cause via crate::pg::err_input(&format!("theodb.graph_refold: lookup failed: {e:?}")); keep the 'run graph_build first' message ONLY for the Ok(None) no-row case. Apply the same distinction at l.383 and l.396.

findings.evidence: load_cached_csr keys the thread_local cache by (oid, epoch=built_at μs) and only returns a hit `if *ep == epoch` (l390-394); graph_refold rewrites built_at with clock_timestamp() so a same-txn refold changes the epoch and refreshes the cache (l351, tested l660-687). CSR persisted as a WAL-logged/MVCC bytea catalog row (l7-10, l347-354).
findings.message: Caching — addressed: the per-backend CSR cache is invalidated correctly via a built_at epoch key (a graph_refold transparently busts it); durability delegates to WAL-logged bytea

findings.evidence: `grep -n 'Some((o?, e?))' graph.rs` -> line 384: `        .and_then(|(o, e)| Some((o?, e?)))` (preceded by `.ok()` on line 383). `o` and `e` are `Option<Oid>`/`Option<i64>`; `o.zip(e)` yields the identical `Option<(Oid, i64)>`.
findings.message: graph.rs:384 uses `.and_then(|(o, e)| Some((o?, e?)))` to combine two `Option`s into an `Option<(Oid, i64)>`. The idiomatic combinator for 'both-Some-or-None' is `Option::zip` (stable since Rust 1.46): `.and_then(|(o, e)| o.zip(e))`. The `Some((o?, e?))` form re-implements `zip` by hand via the try-operator, which is less clear than naming the intent. Idiomatic form side-by-side — current: `.and_then(|(o, e)| Some((o?, e?)))`; idiomatic: `.and_then(|(o, e)| o.zip(e))`.
findings.remediation: Replace `.and_then(|(o, e)| Some((o?, e?)))` with `.and_then(|(o, e)| o.zip(e))`.

findings.evidence: l139-142 `let dim = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[0..4]...) as usize; let bits = bytes[4]; let need = 5 + dim * dim * 4; if bytes.len() != need { return Err(...) }`. `dim` comes from the codebook's own header (read via read_chunked of the v8 rabitq_codebook region, am/scan.rs: 1147 / am/page/ivf.rs read_ivf_aq_meta_split_rabitq). For dim near u32::MAX, `dim*dim*4` overflows usize (release: wraps; debug: panics); a wrapped `need` colliding with the real bytes.len() constructs a quantizer with a huge `dim` and a short `rotation` Vec, then rotate() l62 `&self.rotation[i*d..(i+1)*d]` indexes OOB -> panic. Requires a crafted corrupt codebook; realistic impact is a panic (DoS).
findings.message: PRINCIPLE (integer-overflow guard on an attacker-influenced size): RabitqQuantizer::from_meta_bytes computes `need = 5 + dim*dim*4` from a disk-read `dim` (u32) without checked arithmetic; a corrupt v8 RaBitQ codebook with a huge dim wraps the product, so the length-equality guard can be bypassed and a later rotate() indexes OOB. Tainted flow: on-disk RaBitQ codebook bytes -> from_meta_bytes dim -> rotate().
findings.remediation: Use checked arithmetic: `let need = dim.checked_mul(dim).and_then(|x| x.checked_mul(4)).and_then(|x| x.checked_add(5)).ok_or("theodb rabitq: meta dim overflow")?;` before the length comparison.

findings.evidence: `ls src/*.rs | wc -l` = 27 loose files at the crate root; vectorizer/embed/chunk/ai_op/rerank are all flat despite forming one cohesive embedding-pipeline concern.
findings.message: vectorizer.rs — a substantial subsystem (background embedding worker + pipeline) — sits loose in a flat `src/` root that already holds 27 top-level .rs files. Its collaborators in the AI/embedding pipeline (embed.rs, chunk.rs, ai_op.rs, rerank.rs) are equally loose. A crowded flat root reduces findability and hides the AI-pipeline package that the code implicitly forms.
findings.remediation: Group the embedding/vectorizer pipeline under `src/ai/` (vectorizer.rs, embed.rs, chunk.rs, ai_op.rs, rerank.rs) to shrink the flat root and make the pipeline a discoverable package.

findings.evidence: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... vectorizer_queue_pending_uniq ON theodb.vectorizer_queue (vectorizer_id, source_pk) WHERE state = 'pending'` (l65-67) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING/UPDATE on enqueue (l92,l97) — 'the single worker cannot be flooded past the number of distinct rows that actually changed.'
findings.message: Backpressure/Message Queue — addressed: producer flooding is bounded by a coalescing partial-unique index (at most one pending job per (vectorizer_id, source_pk))

findings.evidence: theodb.vectorizer_stats() returns processed/failed/last_run + live pending/processing/failed counts (l173-181); the worker bumps theodb.vectorizer_worker_stats via _vectorizer_bump_stats each poll (l1079-1084).
findings.message: Metrics Collection — addressed: the worker exposes a queryable throughput + queue-depth metric (not just log lines)

findings.evidence: _vectorizer_mark_done deletes only `WHERE job_id=$1 AND owner=$2 AND state='processing'` (l259-261); a false return means the lease was lost and the caller MUST discard its result (H1 fencing). owner is a per-incarnation uuid (l1027-1032).
findings.message: Idempotency — addressed: every completion/failure transition is fenced by a globally-unique owner token so a reclaimed job cannot be clobbered by a stale worker

findings.evidence: _vectorizer_mark_failed: `state = CASE WHEN attempts >= $4 THEN 'failed' ELSE 'pending' END` with `lease_deadline = ... now() + make_interval(secs => least(power(2, least(attempts,12))::int, 300))` (l291-296); attempts burned ON CLAIM (l222) so a job that kills the worker still counts down to the failed dead-letter (H3).
findings.message: Retry — addressed: bounded attempts + exponential backoff + dead-letter (never an infinite retry loop)

findings.evidence: upsert_chunks l383 `let chunk_tbl = format!("{}_chunks", cfg.target_table);` then l385 `let del = format!("DELETE FROM {chunk_tbl} WHERE source_pk = $1")` and l394-395 `INSERT INTO {chunk_tbl} ...`; _vectorizer_process_delete l468 repeats `format!("DELETE FROM {}_chunks ...", cfg.target_table)`. cfg.target_table is loaded from theodb.vectorizer (lookup_config l363). MITIGATION VERIFIED: create_vectorizer types the param `target_table regclass` (l109) and stores `target_table` into a text column via INSERT l131-132, so the value is regclass::text (a real, SQL-escaped, schema-qualified relation name) — not arbitrary user text, so injection is not reachable today (a crafted relation name is already quoted). Residual risk: (a) raw `{}_chunks` suffix appended OUTSIDE the regclass quoting produces a broken/mismatched token for relations needing quoting; (b) the in-place path deliberately routes tables through format()'s `%s` with the same regclass-safe arg, so the chunk path is an inconsistent bypass that would become a real CWE-89 if target_table storage changed to raw text. build_sql's `$fmt${template}$fmt$` (l419) is safe because `template` is always a hardcoded string literal at every call site.
findings.message: PRINCIPLE (least-astonishment / route every identifier through the same quoting path): the chunk-table mode builds the target table name with a RAW Rust `format!("{}_chunks", cfg.target_table)` and interpolates it directly into SQL, bypassing the parameterized `%I`/regclass-`%s`-via-format path the in-place mode (build_sql) uses. Currently mitigated because target_table is stored as regclass::text, but it is a latent injection if that storage type ever changes.
findings.remediation: Route the chunk-table name through the same format()/quote path: resolve `format('%I', (target||'_chunks'))` server-side, or store+use `quote_ident(target_table||'_chunks')`, rather than raw Rust `format!("{}_chunks")` interpolation.

findings.evidence: The fetch template `"SELECT %1$I::text FROM %2$s WHERE %3$I::text = $1"` is repeated in _vectorizer_process_upsert (l435), _vectorizer_process_upsert_batch (l506) and _vectorizer_read_batch (l572); the update template `"UPDATE %2$s SET %1$I = $1::vector WHERE %3$I::text = $2"` in _vectorizer_process_upsert (l451), _upsert_batch (l533) and _write_batch (l597).
findings.message: DRY: the fetch/update dynamic-SQL templates (built via build_sql over cfg.content_col/target_col/source_table/target_table/source_pk_col) are re-typed as string literals across five vectorizer functions. A change to the fetch/upsert shape (e.g. adding a WHERE guard) must be edited in each copy, risking drift between the single-txn and 3-phase paths.
findings.remediation: Add two `VecCfg` methods (or const templates) `fetch_sql(&self)` / `upsert_sql(&self)` that call build_sql once; the five entrypoints reuse them.

findings.evidence: _vectorizer_reap_orphans dead-letters jobs stuck at the attempt cap (l631-646); _vectorizer_purge_dead_letters keeps only the most recent `keep` failed rows (l654-668, default theodb.vectorizer_dead_letter_max=1000); both run in the worker's periodic reap_and_purge (l829-841).
findings.message: Disaster Recovery/bounded state — addressed: orphan reaper + bounded on-disk dead-letter prevent unbounded failed-row accumulation

findings.evidence: ON CONFLICT (vectorizer_id, source_pk) WHERE state='pending' DO UPDATE (coalesce) at l.92/97; exponential backoff `least(power(2, least(attempts,12))::int, 300)` at l.295; dead-letter `state = CASE WHEN attempts >= $4 THEN 'failed' ELSE 'pending' END` at l.292; owner-guarded predicate `WHERE job_id=$1 AND owner=$2 AND state='processing'` at l.296; FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED at l.228.
findings.message: Transactional Outbox + Retry-with-Backoff + Dead-Letter + Idempotency/fencing — applied_correctly: the AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger `_vectorizer_enqueue` (l.81) writes the job into `theodb.vectorizer_queue` in the SAME transaction as the source change and does only a cheap INSERT (no HTTP), with the async worker as the relay — the Outbox pattern. `_vectorizer_mark_failed` (l.277) implements bounded exponential backoff (`least(power(2, least(attempts,12))::int, 300)`) with an attempt cap that dead-letters to state='failed' (never an infinite retry). Every state transition is fenced by a globally-unique `owner` uuid (`WHERE job_id=$1 AND owner=$2 AND state='processing'`) so a reclaimed-lease worker cannot clobber the new owner (Idempotency/fencing), and a coalescing partial unique index (l.65) is producer backpressure. `claim_batch` uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (Producer-Consumer over the DB queue). A faithful resilience/messaging implementation that earns its complexity — no misapplied pattern in this file. [pattern+source: Hohpe & Woolf EIP 2003 (Transactional Outbox, at-least-once implies idempotent receivers) + Nygard Release It! 2018 (Retry+Backoff / Dead-Letter) — applied_correctly.]
